Plan attention
before the event.

Agree on what the team needs to learn, what each person will investigate, and what evidence will return.

What must we learn to move the work forward?

  • What decision, next step, or problem does this learning need to inform?
  • What do we need to understand, see, or find out that we do not yet know?

Start with a production need. A sketch or a plain sentence can make it visible.

Team purpose

Our purpose is to transform our original Pilot Cat concept into an entertaining, interactive Unity game using the three Pipelines: Important Information, The Beginning, and Storytelling. We aim to develop Pilot Cat's 1930s-inspired world, characters, and adventures while understanding the information, planning, and creative decisions needed to bring the story to life. Through teamwork, Unity development, and C# programming, we will create a playable experience that every team member can understand, demonstrate, and explain.

Working agreement and individual attention brief

Each person names what they will investigate, what they need to understand, what they will capture and return, and how the team will use it. Focus questions are temporary; they do not divide required core work among members.

Use current strengths and a learning stretch. Learner, developer, architect, collaborator and orchestrator are ways to direct attention, not fixed ranks or labels.

Contribution, solo work and sharing

A failed experiment with a clear explanation, evidence and next step is a useful contribution. Compare what each person promised with what they returned; a folder name alone is not evidence. Discuss missing contributions and document any decision to continue separately. Preserve and credit prior work; in a course, the instructor retains grading authority.

Solo work uses the same purpose, focus, capture and return process. You do not need a team repository. This file works offline and does not synchronize between people. Share a saved copy or agree on one person to combine the records.

Every learner keeps a personal form, project, notes, whiteboard and evidence in their personal GitHub. If grouped, cross-link team work. Everyone explains the whole. Submit the personal GitHub URL to Canvas Action 12A.
